title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in Illinois
description: Illinois voters will elect one U.S. senator in 2026 to fill the Class II seat held by Dick Durbin, who is not seeking re-election. The open seat makes this one of the state’s most consequential contests, with the outcome likely to reflect Illinois’ strong Democratic lean in a race that will still draw national attention. The Democratic primary is expected to be the main battleground, while the general election will likely center on party control, turnout, and candidates’ positions on the economy, abortion, and federal governance.
polling_note: Public polling in the Illinois Senate race has been limited and has focused on the Democratic primary. Available recent polling includes a March 3, 2026 Public Policy Polling survey of Democratic primary voters.

candidates.name: Juliana Stratton
candidates.summary: Juliana Stratton is the lieutenant governor of Illinois and the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2026. Her campaign says she is running on a platform centered on affordability, opportunity, and protecting rights and freedoms.

summary_sources.title: Fighting for Illinois | Juliana Stratton for U.S. Senate

Healthcare.stance: Supports securing Medicare for All and lowering healthcare costs; her campaign says she wants families to be able to afford care without skipping medication and highlights efforts to relieve medical debt in Illinois.

Climate/Energy.stance: Supports urgent action on climate change and says she has fought for environmental protections in Illinois as part of her broader rights-and-freedoms agenda.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Supports restoring the abortion protections of Roe v. Wade and protecting reproductive freedom, including access to abortion and contraception.

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Supports common-sense gun safety laws and says she wants to tackle gun violence as a public safety and public health issue.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Supports protecting voting rights, safeguarding LGBTQ+ rights, and defending civil liberties as part of her rights-and-democracy agenda.

sources.title: Juliana's Priorities - Protecting Your Rights and Our Democracy

Immigration.stance: Supports abolishing ICE and replacing it with an immigration system that emphasizes judges, community-based resources, social services, and a pathway to citizenship.

Education.stance: Supports restoring the Department of Education, expanding support for trades and technical schools, investing in early childhood programs, increasing public school funding, and addressing teacher shortages.

Tech & AI.stance: Supports workforce training and education policies to help workers adapt to AI and automation, including expanded technical-skills training and related Pell Grant support.

sources.title: UChicago Institute of Politics on AI and the workplace (Stratton)

Election Policy.stance: Supports strong federal voting-rights protections, including the John Lewis Voting Rights Act, and says she wants to expand access to the ballot.

Local Issues.stance: Says she will focus on making life more affordable for Illinois families, citing her work as lieutenant governor on the grocery tax, minimum wage, and medical debt relief, and pledges to carry that focus into the Senate.

Economy.stance: Supports raising the federal minimum wage, ending Trump-era trade policies she says hurt working families, and cutting taxes for the middle class while increasing taxes on people making more than $1 million a year.

career_history.title: State Representative
career_history.description: Previously served in the Illinois House.

candidates.voting_summary: Juliana Stratton has not held legislative office, so there is no legislative voting record to report. She is Illinois lieutenant governor, and public official pages describe her executive portfolio as leading state initiatives rather than casting votes; Vote Smart also lists her issue positions and candidate profile rather than a legislative roll call record.
candidates.donor_summary: Juliana Stratton’s 2026 Senate campaign has raised millions in receipts, with most money coming from individual donors and additional support from other committees. Prior fundraising data show labor unions as a major source of support, and news reports say Gov. JB Pritzker gave $5 million through a pro-Stratton super PAC.

candidates.name: Chad Koppie
candidates.summary: Chad Koppie is the Constitution Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Illinois. His campaign website presents him as a farmer and retired pilot and says he is running on a platform of limited government, lower debt, and socially conservative positions.

Healthcare.stance: Koppie says he is a free-market advocate and that government should protect the freedom to choose in health care. His campaign materials also call for health care reform along free-market lines.

Economy.stance: Koppie says an out-of-control national debt and deficit oppresses the economy and prevents economic growth. His campaign emphasizes reducing debt and deficits and supporting pro-growth, limited-government policies.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Koppie describes himself as pro-life and supports a constitutional view that life begins at conception. His campaign materials indicate opposition to abortion.

sources.title: Illinois Right To Life Action 2026 voter guide – Chad Koppie

Foreign Policy.stance: Koppie says the federal government should conduct relations with other nations on behalf of the states and emphasizes U.S. sovereignty in foreign policy.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Koppie says the primary purpose of government is to protect the rights and liberties of the people. His campaign frames civil liberties as a foundational government responsibility.

Education.stance: Koppie says the federal government has no constitutional authority over public education and calls for education control to be returned to states and local authorities.

Immigration.stance: Koppie says immigration control is a fundamental sovereign power. His campaign opposes amnesty, sanctuary policies, and state laws that allow undocumented immigrants to receive benefits such as driver's licenses or in-state tuition.

Election Policy.stance: Koppie’s campaign materials include an election reform section, but no detailed public position was found in the available pages reviewed.

Local Issues.stance: Koppie’s website does not present a detailed local-issues agenda in the materials reviewed; his campaign instead emphasizes constitutional limits on federal power and local control over education and immigration enforcement.

forecast.rationale: This is an open-seat race in a state described in the race profile as having a strong Democratic lean. The listed Democratic nominee, Juliana Stratton, is a statewide elected official with substantial fundraising support, while the only other listed nominee is a Constitution Party candidate with no evident financial base or prior elected profile. Public polling in the race is very limited and the available poll referenced here focused on the Democratic primary rather than a general-election matchup, so the forecast relies mainly on Illinois’s partisan context and the relative strength of the listed candidates rather than direct general-election polling. That supports a strong Democratic advantage, though confidence is reduced somewhat by sparse general-election data and the possibility of an eventual Republican nominee not reflected in the current candidate list.
